title: Multimodal Weak-Supervision Evaluation & Augmentation Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a repeatable process for constructing, augmenting, and evaluating multimodal (text + image / layout / audio) workloads using weak supervision signals. It is intended for ML engineers and evaluation owners who are onboarding models that accept or produce multimodal outputs, and for teams responsible for regression triage and embedding/quantization stability tests.

Goals:
- Define a defensible, low-cost pipeline for generating labeled multimodal test sets using weak supervision sources (heuristics, retrieval, synthetic generators).
- Provide annotation and adjudication guidance to ensure high signal-to-noise in critical slices.
- Integrate multimodal tests into the eval harness with clear pass/fail criteria and quantization sensitivity checks.
- Provide a rapid triage path for regressions that surface on augmented slices.

Scope and constraints:
- Works for: image+caption, document PDF layout+text, video-keyframe+transcript, and audio+transcript evaluation flows.
- Not intended for: full end-to-end multimodal dataset labeling at scale (use an MDS program for that). This playbook prioritizes targeted slices where weak supervision buys >10x labeling efficiency.

Definitions:
- Weak supervision sources: heuristics, programmatic labeling functions, model-derived pseudo-labels, retrieval heuristics from existing corpora.
- Slice: a semantically coherent subset of traffic (e.g., receipts with small fonts, hand-written forms, low-light images).
- Anchor examples: high-confidence human-labeled examples used to calibrate weak labels.

High-level process (summary):
1. Define target slices and acceptance metrics.
2. Assemble seed corpus and weak supervision functions.
3. Generate pseudo-labeled candidates and score label confidence.
4. Select stratified samples for human annotation and anchoring.
5. Calibrate and synthesize augmented prompt/perturbation variants.
6. Integrate into eval harness, run baseline and quantized variants.
7. Monitor slice-level metrics; trigger regression triage when thresholds are crossed.

1) Slice definition and acceptance metrics
- Owner: evaluation lead (example: @eval-lead).
- For each slice, record: name, description, cardinality estimate, priority (P0–P3), success metrics.
- Example slice table (markdown):
| slice | description | estimate | priority | primary metric | threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| low-light-images | photos with avg luminance < 0.15 | ~12k | P0 | grounding_precision@0.9 | >0.88 |
| tiny-font-receipts | receipts with font-size < 8pt | ~3k | P1 | ocr_character_f1 | >0.92 |

Primary metrics (examples):
- grounding_precision: fraction of generated references that correctly localize image regions / assets.
- alignment_f1: for structured outputs (tables, forms) compare predicted spans to reference spans via F1.
- hallucination_rate: percent of responses containing non-supported facts (determined by anchor verification).
- retrieval_ndcg@k: relevance for retrieval-backed captioning or context insertion.
- tokenized_error_rate: for transcriptions and OCR.

2) Weak supervision sources and scoring
- Types: heuristic (regex/OCR heuristics), retrieval (nearest-neighbor from labeled seed), model pseudo-labels (teacher models), synthetic (rendered templates / TTS / image perturbations).
- Each source must emit: label, confidence_score (0–1), provenance tag.
- Combine using a simple calibrated aggregator (logistic stacking or majority voting with source weights).
- Minimal metadata for a weak label must include: source_name, label_schema_version, confidence, seed_anchor_id (if derived).

3) Candidate generation and confidence calibration
- Use the following pipeline:
  a. Pull seed corpus (specify query or dataset id).
  b. Apply labeling functions in parallel, collect outputs.
  c. Compute source-level reliability using anchor examples; derive calibrated confidence (Platt scaling or isotonic regression recommended).
  d. Assign final pseudo-labels and stratify by confidence bucket: high (>0.85), medium (0.6–0.85), low (<0.6).

YAML example for labeling function registration (include in eval-harness config):
```yaml
labeling_functions:
  - id: regex-amount-usd
    type: heuristic
    description: "extract monetary amounts preceded by $ or USD"
    params: {pattern: "(?<=\$)\\d+(?:\\.\\d{2})?"}
    weight: 0.6
  - id: teacher-captioner-v2
    type: model
    model_ref: "models/vision-caption/teacher-v2@2025-10-01"
    weight: 0.9
```

4) Annotation and adjudication protocol
- Target throughput: annotate 200-500 anchors per slice initially.
- Annotation roles:
  - Annotator: apply label schema to sample items; mark uncertainties.
  - Adjudicator: resolves disagreements for anchor set; documents decision rationale.
  - Reviewer: periodic quality audit (10% random sample).
- Annotation guidelines must include: clear pass/fail criteria, examples of borderline cases, and a short checklist for each item.
- Dispute resolution: when annotator/adjudicator disagree > 8% across a batch, pause and update labeling functions.

Label schema example (flat list encoded as JSON lines in the annotation tool):
- label_id: grounding_ok
  description: "Model correctly identifies image region(s) referenced in text."
- label_id: partial_grounding
  description: "Some referenced regions correct, but missing others."
- label_id: hallucination
  description: "Output asserts content not present in the image or document."

5) Augmentation and perturbation generation
- Augmentations: scale/rotate_crop, synthetic_noise (jpeg/artifacts), contrast_low, OCR_blur, paraphrase_text, context_dropout (remove retrieved context to test hallucination).
- For each augmentation, define an expected metric delta tolerance (e.g., grounding_precision drop < 0.06 for P0 slices).
- When applying augmentations, preserve anchor IDs and provenance so regressions can be traced.

6) Integration with the eval harness
- Create a harness job per slice with the following knobs: model_variant, quant_setting, batch_profile, inference_timeout_ms.
- Example CLI run (eval harness):
  ./eval-harness run --suite multimodal/low-light-images.yaml --model-ref models/multi/serving-v3 --quant=8bitq

- Required outputs from harness: per-example predictions, per-example confidence, slice-level aggregated metrics, per-perturbation breakdown, and a compact diagnostics bundle (top-20 failure examples with metadata).

7) Quantization and runtime sensitivity checks
- For each slice run: fp16 (baseline), int8-quant (profiled), q4_0 (if supported). Compare primary metrics and compute sensitivity score:
  sensitivity = max(0, baseline_metric - quant_metric) / baseline_metric.
- Thresholds: sensitivity >= 0.10 for P0 slices triggers an investigation.
- If quantization increases hallucination_rate by > 5 percentage points, mark as high risk and block auto-promotion.

8) Regression detection and triage flow
- Alerting: slice-level metrics are pushed to RedMetrics. Create alerts when:
  - metric delta > threshold for consecutive 3 runs, or
  - a single run contains >0.5% of traffic with confidence < 0.2 and a matching failure signature.
- Triage quick-path (15–30 minute):
  1. Confirm failure in eval harness using the model commit hash.
 2. Compare anchor examples: did anchors flip labels? If yes, rollback candidate change.
  3. Run quantization-free baseline to check if error is quant-induced.
  4. Check weak supervision provenance: did a labeling function drift?
  5. If not resolved, escalate to regression team with diagnostics bundle.

9) Promotion and canary rules
- Promotion gating: a slice fails promotion if any P0 slice metric is below threshold OR quantization sensitivity > limits.
- Canary rollout plan: 20% traffic for 24h -> 50% for 24h -> full rollout, with slice-level monitoring at each step. Auto-fallback policy: revert to previous model if any P0 slice metric regresses > 0.05 absolute.

10) Ownership, roles and SLAs
- Evaluation lead: owns slice definitions, acceptance thresholds (SLA: respond to triage within 24h).
- Regression on-call: 4-person rotation in eng-platform; SLA: initial investigation within 2h for P0 alerts.
- Annotation ops: manage annotation throughput and anchor quality; SLA: replenish anchors weekly for high-traffic slices.

Appendix A — Example failure diagnostics bundle fields (CSV friendly):
- example_id, slice, augmentation_tag, model_ref, quant_setting, baseline_metric, current_metric, confidence, labeling_provenance, anchor_label, annotator_notes

Appendix B — Quick checklist before trusting weak labels for promotion:
- Anchor coverage >= 200 examples per P0 slice.
- Weighted aggregator AUC >= 0.92 on anchor holdout.
- No single source >80% of labels unless source is verified teacher model.
- Documentation for each labeling function present in the eval-harness config.

Appendix C — Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Mode: heuristic overfitting (heuristic matches artifacts of training data). Mitigation: randomize and add negative examples to seed.
- Mode: retrieval mismatch (retrieved context from wrong domain). Mitigation: domain-aware retrieval filters and reranking.
- Mode: quantization-induced hallucination. Mitigation: force higher-precision for decoding layer or apply targeted calibration.
